learn.title: Reliability, predictability, security, governance and manageability
objectives: Describe how the cloud improves reliability and resilience.
Describe performance predictability and cost predictability.
Describe the security benefits of cloud services.
Describe how governance keeps resources compliant with standards.
Describe manageability: management of the cloud and management in the cloud.
concepts: Reliability
The ability of a system to recover from failures and keep working. The cloud's global footprint and redundancy make this easier.
Decentralised design
Spreading resources across zones and regions so there's no single point of failure.
Performance predictability
Consistent performance under changing load, using autoscaling, load balancing and high availability.
Cost predictability
Forecasting and tracking spending with the pricing calculator, Microsoft Cost Management and budgets.
Autoscaling
Automatically adding or removing resources based on demand or a schedule.
Load balancing
Spreading traffic across several instances and routing it away from unhealthy ones.
Security benefits
PaaS and SaaS patch for you, encryption at rest is on by default for Azure Storage, plus built-in protection at scale.
Governance
Rules and standards that keep deployments compliant: Azure Policy, resource locks, templates, tags and audit logs.
Management of the cloud
Managing the resources themselves: scaling, template deployment, health monitoring, alerts.
Management in the cloud
The ways you manage: Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, REST APIs, the mobile app.
comparisons: Reliability is about recovering from failure. Predictability is about knowing how performance and cost will behave.
Policy controls what resources and settings are allowed. RBAC controls who can perform actions.
Policy enforces configuration rules. Locks stop accidental deletion or changes, even by owners.
The calculator estimates costs before deployment. Budgets track real spending and send alerts.
traps: Budgets alert you. They don't stop resources by themselves.
Replication copies deletions too, so backups are still needed.
The pricing calculator gives estimates, not your actual bill.
An Audit policy effect reports non-compliance but doesn't block it.
Reliability doesn't mean failures never happen.
revision: Zones protect against a datacenter failure. Multiple regions protect against a region failure.
Autoscale plus a load balancer gives predictable performance.
Pricing calculator, Cost Management and budgets give predictable cost.
PaaS and SaaS shift patching to Microsoft.
Policy = what is allowed. RBAC = who can act. Locks = prevent delete or change.
The Activity log shows who did what and when.
